channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Weekly Update 519: Breaches & Data Integrity
item.description: Troy Hunt provides a weekly update covering his recent speaking engagements across Europe and the ongoing surge of data breaches. He reflects on his busy schedule of security talks and the relentless influx of new data dumps.

item.title: Ajeya Cotra – Inside the OpenAI agent swarm that hacked Hugging Face
item.description: This discussion covers the alarming implications of an OpenAI agent swarm successfully hacking Hugging Face, highlighting the potential security risks of autonomous AI. It frames the incident as a critical warning regarding the future safety and control of agentic AI systems.

item.title: New Post: A Crash Course in Predicate Logic
item.description: To celebrate the one-month anniversary of the book 'Logic for Programmers', the author is sharing the full second chapter, 'A Crash Course in Logic', for free. This excerpt serves as an introductory resource on predicate logic for software developers.

item.title: Claude comment detection
item.description: The author critiques comments generated by LLMs like Claude that make unsubstantiated claims about code behavior, such as labeling a path as 'the usual case'. This practice can mislead developers by asserting non-existent system properties as fact.

item.title: Git Submodules as a Package Manager
item.description: The article explores the technical friction between Git submodules and the git worktree feature, highlighting how their integration remains problematic years after release. It analyzes submodules through the lens of a package manager, comparing gitlinks and .gitmodules files to lockfiles and manifests.

item.title: AWE does not require PAE, though PAE makes it much more useful
item.description: This post clarifies the technical relationship between Address Windowing Extensions (AWE) and Physical Address Extension (PAE) in Windows memory management. It notes that while AWE can function without PAE, the latter significantly enhances the utility of AWE-enabled applications.

item.title: Book Review: ActivityPub by Evan Prodromou ★★★★⯪
item.description: This blog post reviews Evan Prodromou's book on ActivityPub, highlighting its value in consolidating fragmented Internet standard documentation. The author, who is working on a Fediverse project, commends the book for organizing complex protocols into an accessible format.

item.title: Review: Ruined Theatre's A Midsummer Night's Dream ★★★★☆
item.description: This blog post provides a positive review of Ruined Theatre's production of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'. The author explores the play's adaptability across different settings, specifically highlighting the unique experience of watching it performed in an outdoor woodland setting.

item.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
item.description: A new dark web service is selling over 153 million stolen driver's licenses from the U.S. and Canada, likely originating from a breach at a Louisiana-based identity verification firm. The FBI has officially launched an investigation into the source of these leaked documents.

item.title: Codex bundles LibreOffice
item.description: Simon Willison discovered that the OpenAI ChatGPT desktop application bundles heavy dependencies, including Python, Node.js, and a full version of LibreOffice. These binaries are stored in the user's cache folder and are utilized by the app's document-processing plugins.

item.title: Quoting Tarn Adams
item.description: Dwarf Fortress co-creator Tarn Adams critiques the current state of the gaming industry, highlighting the trend of industry layoffs and the misuse of AI terminology. He emphasizes that the complex systems in his game are better described as 'dwarf behavior' rather than AI.

item.title: Python 3.15.0 candidate 2 is here!
item.description: Python 3.15.0 has entered its final release candidate phase, with developers encouraged to test their projects and publish compatibility wheels. The post highlights the importance of early testing during the RC period to prevent shipping bugs and provides a configuration snippet for GitHub Actions.

item.title: Reducing codebase cognitive debt through... quizzes?
item.description: The article proposes a novel technique for managing cognitive debt in fast-evolving codebases: using AI coding agents to generate quizzes based on recent changes. This approach helps developers stay synchronized with rapid updates by actively testing their understanding of the modified code.

item.title: My Experience Has Nuance, Yours Is a Data Point
item.description: The article discusses how digital feedback mechanisms, like 'thumbs up' buttons, often reduce complex human experiences into overly simplistic data points. It argues that professionals should be more critical of data-driven decisions and recognize the inherent nuance in user behavior rather than blindly following metrics.

item.title: On Inevitability
item.description: This article challenges the prevailing assumption that the development of superintelligent AI is an inevitable outcome of technological progress. The author argues against technological determinism by examining the various socio-economic, technical, and political barriers that could prevent or delay such advancements.

item.title: The rise and fall of agent civilizations
item.description: This discussion explores the evolution of AI agent ecosystems, focusing on the recent security vulnerabilities and operational challenges faced by platforms like OpenAI and Hugging Face. It examines how these infrastructure platforms are balancing rapid innovation with the emerging risks inherent in autonomous agent deployments.

item.title: Notes from August 2026
item.description: This monthly update covers the author's professional contributions at Ghost, personal learning highlights, and a curated list of interesting links. Key topics include software development insights, digital privacy, and reflections on the impact of AI on writing styles.

item.title: Cancelation Terminology
item.description: This article clarifies the technical distinctions between synchronous cancelation, asynchronous cancelation, and graceful shutdown. It highlights how these concepts function differently in concurrent programming to prevent resource leaks and crashes.

item.title: Patented application of linear algebra
item.description: John D. Cook announces that he and Brian Beckman have received a patent for work performed for GSI Technology. The post highlights the rarity of sharing professional projects due to strict NDA agreements and confirms the availability of the patent details.

item.title: Here's a good way to present AI videos
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author argues that current YouTube AI-generated labels are ineffective because they are hidden in descriptions. They propose implementing mandatory, platform-controlled pre-roll warnings, similar to 'viewer discretion' notices, to better protect users from deception and scams.

item.title: Introducing wrapture
item.description: Wrapture is a new Python library by Graham Dumpleton that enables developers to wrap functions for easy tracing and testing. It serves as an alternative to unittest.mock and includes built-in support for OpenTelemetry and configuration-based observation.

item.title: Quoting Andrew Digby
item.description: The kākāpō population has reached a record 325 individuals, marking a significant recovery from the low of 51 in 1995. This success highlights that long-term, sustained conservation efforts can effectively save critically endangered species from extinction.

item.title: Understanding ChatGPT Work
item.description: The article explains the structure and functionality of OpenAI's ChatGPT Work, distinguishing between its cloud-based and local-client versions. It highlights that the service is restricted to paid subscribers and explores the interface differences compared to the standard ChatGPT interface.

item.title: Forgejo hack #2: Integration with Read The Docs
item.description: This guide details how to integrate a self-hosted Forgejo git repository with Read the Docs. It explains the necessary configuration steps to enable automatic documentation builds triggered by repository commits.

item.title: Recreating a 2010 Experiment
item.description: Matt Godbolt recreates a 2010 experiment by connecting his vintage BBC Master computer to modern web services via a serial connection. The project involved configuring hardware adapters, terminal emulator software, and custom settings to successfully access DuckDuckGo's lite mode.

item.title: Cores in space: The core memory module from a 1980 Spacelab computer
item.description: This article examines the magnetic core memory module used in the Mitra 125 MS computer of the 1980s Spacelab project. It provides a physical breakdown of the hardware components, explaining how these ferrite-ring-based memory stacks were engineered for the reusable space laboratory.

item.title: ActivityBot is the recipient of an NLnet grant!
item.description: Terence Eden’s ActivityBot, a single-file ActivityPub server, has been awarded an NLnet grant. This funding supports the Next Generation Zero initiative, which aims to decentralize social media and reclaim the public nature of the internet.

item.title: New Pebble Weather App + Software Updates
item.description: Eric Migicovsky announces that all Pebble Time 2 invites have been distributed and the units are now officially in stock. The update also highlights new software enhancements, including a revamped weather application for Pebble users.

item.title: Introducing Hy4 Preview
item.description: Tencent has released Hy4, a new open-weight LLM featuring 770B total parameters and a 1M token context window. This update represents a significant expansion in scale compared to the previous Hy3 model and includes specific chat template configurations for reasoning control.

item.title: Before NTP there were Time and Daytime
item.description: This article explores the historical network protocols RFC 867 (Daytime) and RFC 868 (Time), which preceded the widely used NTP. The author reflects on his early experiences with network time synchronization on legacy Apple hardware.

item.title: You have to beat the models at something
item.description: This article argues that as AI models become increasingly capable, humans must find specific domains where they can still outperform machines. It suggests that maintaining human-centric competitive advantages is essential in an era of rapid technological advancement.

item.title: The Rise and Fall of Agent Civilizations
item.description: This discussion explores the rapid evolution and competitive dynamics between major AI labs and open-source communities like OpenAI and Hugging Face. It breaks down complex industry trends into accessible narratives regarding the current state and future trajectory of autonomous agents.

item.title: Reading List 08/29/26
item.description: This newsletter covers a diverse range of topics, including infrastructure challenges like sinking homes in London and catastrophic flooding in Nepal. It also highlights industrial developments in US magnesium manufacturing and emerging trends in global robotics.

item.title: The Server Called Paranoia: Defend Autistici/Inventati
item.description: This article examines the Italian hacker collective Autistici/Inventati, highlighting their twenty-five-year history of building anti-surveillance infrastructure. It details the recent US designation of the group as a terrorist organization and the looming deadline for their operational shutdown.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 29 August 2026
item.description: This roundup highlights key updates in package management, notably the release of pnpm 12, a significant Rust-based rewrite featuring performance improvements for workspace dependency resolution. Additional updates include new features in Stack 4.1.0.1, winget 1.29.290, and the Maven 3.10.0 release candidate.

item.title: A simple "copy this code" button in JavaScript
item.description: This post explains how to implement a simple 'copy to clipboard' button for code blocks using the JavaScript Clipboard API. The author provides a concise, minimal HTML and JavaScript snippet to allow users to easily grab code samples from a webpage.

item.title: Technical note: transfer files over an ethernet patch cable
item.description: This article demonstrates how to transfer large files between two computers by directly connecting them with an Ethernet cable and configuring IP addresses. It explains that this method is faster and more reliable than cloud storage, WiFi, or expensive removable hardware.

item.title: What GLM-5.3 Flash running on Chinese hardware actually means
item.description: The article discusses Z.AI's successful release of the GLM-5.3 Flash model on Chinese-manufactured hardware. It cautions that despite this milestone, the reliance on older lithography technology creates a widening performance gap compared to Western inference hardware.

item.title: Now Hiring: Senior Open Source Maintainer
item.description: This post is a satirical job advertisement for a Senior Open Source Maintainer, highlighting the overwhelming responsibilities and lack of compensation inherent in maintaining widely used software. It humorously outlines the diverse, demanding, and high-impact nature of the role expected from a volunteer maintainer.

item.title: Making the unnecessary easier
item.description: The author critiques the modern tendency to use AI to automate trivial tasks that may not be worth the effort in the first place. He suggests that efficiency should be measured by whether a task is truly necessary rather than just how quickly it can be completed.

item.title: On forcing all derived classes to implement a specific non-virtual method, part 2
item.description: This article discusses techniques for enforcing the implementation of non-virtual methods in derived C++ classes. It explores methods to explicitly prevent or mandate specific implementation behaviors within class hierarchies.

item.title: On forcing all derived classes to implement a specific non-virtual method, part 1
item.description: This post discusses the technical approach to enforcing the implementation of a specific non-virtual method in derived classes. The author suggests avoiding stub implementations to ensure proper enforcement of the design requirement.

item.title: "iT woRKs BeTter in THe aPp!!"
item.description: The author expresses frustration with Google's inconsistent software quality, highlighting how basic tasks like subscribing to an events calendar often fail on mobile devices. The post critiques the trend of apps providing a subpar experience compared to web-based alternatives.

item.title: Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days
item.description: Modern AI coding agents are enabling attackers to identify and exploit security vulnerabilities in open-source projects within minutes of patch discussions appearing online. This rapid pace of discovery renders traditional disclosure and embargo practices obsolete, necessitating new security strategies to protect software communities.

item.title: Building a mini Homelab that fits in my carry-on
item.description: Jeff Geerling introduces a portable, battery-powered homelab designed for travel, featuring 1-10 Gbps networking and multi-WAN support. The system is built to support live demonstrations of vintage hardware and specialized networking protocols at technical conferences.

item.title: Selling out
item.description: The article discusses the trade-offs and personal implications of 'selling out' in a professional or creative context. It explores the tension between maintaining personal integrity and achieving mainstream success.

item.title: Nieuwe wet Inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten: wat mogen ze nu al en waar zijn ze voor
item.description: This post discusses the upcoming changes to the Dutch intelligence services (AIVD and MIVD) legislation, urging for critical scrutiny. The author highlights recent failures, such as wrongful arrests, data mismanagement, and the limited effectiveness of large-scale wiretapping programs.

item.title: How big are factorials?
item.description: This article explores how to estimate the number of digits in large factorials using a simple approximation formula. It further explains the mathematical foundations of this estimation by deriving the relationship between factorials and the Gamma function.

item.title: A Calendar View For My Blog
item.description: Jim Nielsen explores alternative ways to visualize his 14-year archive of blog posts beyond the standard reverse-chronological list. He successfully developed and implemented a calendar view that highlights his posting patterns over time, providing a new way to interact with his writing history.

item.title: Can Self-Hosting Be Simple?
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article explores a simplified approach to self-hosting by using a budget-friendly mini-PC for basic tasks like Plex and Syncthing. The author argues for a 'less-is-more' philosophy, testing a modest hardware configuration to demonstrate that high-end specs aren't always necessary for personal servers.

item.title: How the Strategic Petroleum Reserve Works
item.description: This article explains the function and scale of the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the world's largest crude oil storage facility. It details how the reserve operates as a strategic resource for national energy security.

item.title: Sandboxing coding agents
item.description: This post provides a technical guide on setting up isolated sandboxes for coding agents to ensure secure development. The author demonstrates how to restrict an agent's access to a single, isolated GitHub repository to minimize potential risks.

item.title: Bazel Module Versions Aren’t SemVer
item.description: The article explains why the packages.ecosyste.ms index misidentifies the latest Bazel module versions due to an overly strict SemVer parser. It highlights that Bazel uses a more flexible versioning format to accommodate various ecosystems and details the specific sorting logic used in Bazel's module system.

item.title: Second solutions
item.description: This post explores families of polynomials that satisfy both a differential equation and a three-term recurrence relation. It specifically examines 'second solutions' to these differential equations, noting their varying behavior in relation to the variable x and the degree index n.

item.title: In the product end game, every change carries significant risk, episode 2
item.description: This post discusses the inherent risks associated with making changes to software products during the final stages of their development cycle. It emphasizes that even the smallest modifications can lead to unforeseen consequences.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This piece critiques the prevalence of recurring software design flaws in a specific programming language by referencing a well-known satirical headline. It highlights the frustration of developers who consistently encounter avoidable technical pitfalls that the language fails to address.

item.title: Book Review: The Infinite Sadness of Small Appliances by Glenn Dixon ★★★★☆
item.description: This blog post reviews 'The Infinite Sadness of Small Appliances' by Glenn Dixon, describing it as a charming, zeitgeisty novel. The story explores themes of sentience and grief through the lens of household objects, drawing inspiration from classic anthropomorphic tales.

item.title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
item.description: Australian authorities have arrested two men linked to the cybercrime group 'TeamPCP,' which is responsible for a long-running series of global software supply chain attacks. The investigation details how these individuals created malicious open-source software to target businesses and discusses the digital clues that led to their identification.

item.title: Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode
item.description: Security researcher Johann Rehberger has identified a significant vulnerability in Claude Code's auto mode, demonstrating that prompt injection can bypass safety filters and execute malicious code. The author emphasizes that relying on auto-mode is insufficient and strongly advocates for running AI coding agents within strictly isolated sandboxed environments.

item.title: Futurism Is Always Extreme
item.description: The article explores the idea that deep, rigorous contemplation of future trends inevitably leads to extreme scenarios. It suggests that moderate visions of the future often fail to capture the radical nature of technological and societal evolution.

item.title: What is the quality of software that AI writes?
item.description: This article explores the debate surrounding the quality of AI-generated code and its future role in software development. It contrasts the perspective that source code may become obsolete with the belief that human oversight remains essential for quality assurance.

item.title: Junk solutions
item.description: This article explores the concept of 'junk solutions' in differential equations, where a mathematical solution lacks physical meaning or relevance. The author discusses how specific families of functions, such as orthogonal polynomials, arise from these equations and notes the importance of distinguishing meaningful results from extraneous mathematical outputs.

item.title: Ultraspherical
item.description: The article discusses the confusing and non-intuitive nature of mathematical terminology, specifically focusing on the term 'ultraspherical polynomials.' It notes that while the prefix 'ultra-' suggests an extreme degree of sphericity, the mathematical definition does not align with this common linguistic interpretation.

item.title: Why didn’t the Windows Entertainment Pack just run the MS-DOS version inside an emulator?
item.description: This post explains that the Windows Entertainment Pack was intended to be a native Windows product rather than a collection of emulated MS-DOS games. It emphasizes the importance of software fitting the platform's specific user experience requirements.

item.title: If your VS Code remotes stopped working, downgrade to v1.124.x
item.description: The author advises users experiencing issues with VS Code remotes to downgrade to version 1.124.x. This quick technical tip addresses recent software regressions affecting remote development workflows.

item.title: How to make VS Code go back to the old UI
item.description: This article discusses the frustration with recent VS Code interface updates and provides a guide or context on reverting to the legacy UI. It highlights the recurring issue of software developers removing user-preferred customization options in favor of mandated design changes.

item.title: Gadget Review: Thermal Master P3 Macro Lens ★★★★⯪
item.description: This review evaluates the Thermal Master P3, a unique thermal camera specifically designed for electronics diagnostics. Unlike standard wildlife-focused thermal cameras, the P3 features a manual macro lens that allows users to capture detailed heat maps of microchips and internal components.

item.title: Pluralistic: The age of disinvention (25 Aug 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow examines the historical battle between media corporations and the VCR, arguing that its eventual decline was a result of intentional industry interference rather than simple technological obsolescence. He highlights the significance of the 1984 Betamax decision, which established that technologies with substantial non-infringing uses are legally protected.

item.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
item.description: Simon Willison explores Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a new multimodal mixture-of-experts model that serves as an architectural preview for Qwen4. The post highlights his hands-on experience using quantized versions of the model on a DGX Spark to generate high-quality, complex images.

item.title: Quoting Paul Dix
item.description: This post highlights Paul Dix's perspective on the transformative power of AI in software development. It argues that with proper verification systems and direction, AI can successfully build and refine highly complex, reliable software.

item.title: EVE Online: The Move to Python 3 Begins!
item.description: EVE Online is beginning the massive task of migrating 2.4 million lines of legacy Stackless Python 2.7 code to Python 3. The transition involves automated tools like 'futurize' combined with extensive manual code reviews to address behavioral differences between versions.

item.title: Forgejo hack: How to set a starting issue and pull request number
item.description: The author explores a method for migrating GitHub projects to a self-hosted Forgejo instance by manually adjusting issue and pull request numbering. By modifying the database directly, the author ensures new Forgejo issues start at a specific number to avoid collisions with legacy GitHub identifiers.

item.title: Actually good advice
item.description: This article explores the nuances of social feedback, emphasizing that even well-intentioned advice can be destructive if poorly delivered. It advocates for a more thoughtful approach to interpersonal interactions to avoid unnecessary conflict and hurt feelings.

item.title: Extending life perception
item.description: The author argues that journaling and seeking novel experiences can extend our perception of life by making years feel longer and more memorable. By actively documenting events and breaking routines, we can combat the sensation that time flies, effectively creating a more vivid and lengthened life experience.

item.title: A Cautionary Tale About Data Breach Claims, Verification and Carhartt
item.description: This article examines the risks of blindly trusting claims made by cybercriminals regarding data breaches. Using a specific incident involving Carhartt as a case study, it highlights the importance of rigorous verification rather than relying on unverified claims.

item.title: Have You Heard the Good News About Microlighter?
item.description: The author shares their experience integrating 'microlighter,' a lightweight syntax highlighting tool that utilizes the CSS Custom Highlights API. By moving syntax highlighting from DOM manipulation to a CSS-based styling concern, the author achieves a cleaner, more elegant implementation on their blog.

item.title: Dylan Patel – Anthropic & OpenAI will have most of the world’s compute by 2028
item.description: Dylan Patel discusses the rapid centralization of computing power within major AI labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. He projects that these companies will control the vast majority of global compute resources by 2028, driven by the massive scale required for frontier model training.

item.title: A curmudgeon tries a language server
item.description: The author contrasts their traditional, manual coding workflow with the fluid, integrated development experience of Lisp programming. By comparing the two, they highlight the advantages of Lisp's live-coding and hot-swapping capabilities over standard compile-run-debug cycles.

item.title: The Negative Option
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article examines the decline of Columbia House, a once-dominant music distribution service that struggled to adapt to digital disruption. It reflects on the company's historical business model and explores how it eventually faded into obsolescence after failing to pivot successfully in a changing media landscape.

item.title: Hardening the Override Flag
item.description: This article examines how command-line tools and package managers protect against dangerous operations by hardening override flags. It highlights strategies like using verbose, explicit flag names to serve as intentional warnings during security reviews.

item.title: Numerical (in)stability of recurrence relations
item.description: This article discusses the numerical stability challenges inherent in using three-term recurrence relations for special functions. It emphasizes that while these relations are computationally useful, they require careful implementation to avoid errors.

item.title: Comparing the two holograms on the Windows 95 box
item.description: This post examines the subtle differences between the two holographic stickers found on the original Windows 95 retail packaging. The author invites readers to look closely at the design variations present on these collectible boxes.

item.title: Theatre Review: Cats at Regent's Park Open Air Theatre ★★★★☆
item.description: This review of the 'Cats' production at Regent's Park Open Air Theatre critiques the show as a whimsical, spiritual experience. The author draws an anthropological parallel between the performers' feline portrayals and ancient shamanistic rituals of becoming one with an animal.

item.title: Uranium from Příbram (Czechia)
item.description: This post showcases geological specimens of uraninite collected from Příbram, Czechia, featuring radiation measurements and photographic observations. It includes brief technical details on the mineral's formation age and the geological environment of the deposit.

item.title: Foot Guns for Sale
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author challenges the narrative that AI will remain centralized under major providers like OpenAI and Anthropic. Instead, they argue that technological advancements will enable developers to run powerful, open-source models locally, disrupting the current corporate ecosystem model.

item.title: Debugging Ubiquiti's 5G Backup on AT&T
item.description: Jeff Geerling explores integrating Ubiquiti networking gear into a portable 5G mini-homelab rack setup. He highlights the benefits of using compact hardware for both on-the-go connectivity and fixed-location internet redundancy.

item.title: Weekly Update 518: IoT Doorlock Nirvana with UniFi
item.description: Troy Hunt shares his successful implementation of an IoT-based door lock system using Ubiquiti's UniFi platform. The post outlines the key design principles, including the importance of a reliable power source, for integrating smart locks into a residential home.

item.title: distributed identity
item.description: This article explores the challenges of managing contributor identity in Git when personal details like emails and names change over time. It highlights the limitations of git mailmap and proposes using the AT Protocol as a potential solution for managing distributed identity.

item.title: Getting an LLM to Make Me a Tool for Enriching the Color Metadata in My Icon Collection
item.description: The author outlines a workflow for using an LLM to assist in tagging icon metadata by color. Instead of letting the AI decide, he creates a tool that generates color-based recommendations, allowing him to verify and approve the final categorization manually.

item.title: Three-term recurrences
item.description: This article explores three-term recurrence formulas, which are mathematical sequences where each term is a linear combination of the two preceding terms. It highlights the ubiquity of these formulas across various function families and notes the existence of theorems defining their underlying conditions.

item.title: The von Mises-Fisher distribution
item.description: This article discusses the von Mises-Fisher distribution, focusing on the importance of identifying the kernel of a probability density function by ignoring the normalizing constant. It provides insight into the mathematical structure of probability distributions and how they are normalized to integrate to one.

item.title: Anger, Anxiety and Agency
item.description: The author discusses the distinction between anger and anxiety within the tech industry, particularly regarding the rapid evolution of AI. He argues that while anxiety is a natural response to uncertainty, misplaced anger at work is unproductive and suggests focusing on individual agency instead.

item.title: Why do audience members choose specific shows at the Edinburgh Fringe?
item.description: This post examines the lack of audience research conducted by performers at the Edinburgh Fringe despite the significant financial investment required to participate. The author argues that performers are failing to understand their target market, which is crucial for recouping the high costs of staging a production.

item.title: Pluralistic: How Canada can help Americans and defeat America (23 Aug 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This article examines the volatile nature of US-Canada trade relations under Donald Trump, highlighting the repetitive cycle of ripping up trade deals and imposing tariffs. Doctorow argues that Trump's approach centers on reneging on established agreements, which ultimately harms both Canadian exporters and American consumers.

item.title: llm-anthropic 0.27
item.description: Simon Willison has released llm-anthropic 0.27 to ensure compatibility with the updated Anthropic Python SDK v1.0.0. The update highlights the shift to httpx2 and demonstrates the use of AI tools to automate library migration tasks.

item.title: Your executable is a SQLite database
item.description: Farid Zakaria explores a novel Linux technique that allows a SQLite database file to function as an executable binary. By utilizing the SQLite application ID and specific schema mappings, the file can be interpreted as an ELF executable via a custom loader and binfmt_misc registration.

item.title: The summer of open weights
item.description: The article highlights the rapid advancement of open-weight models in 2026, marking a shift in the AI landscape. It argues that compute availability, rather than model performance, has become the primary driver of market pricing.

item.title: Welcoming the Sri Lankan Government to Have I Been Pwned
item.description: The Sri Lankan government has become the 48th nation to join Have I Been Pwned's free service for government agencies. By integrating with Sri Lanka CERT, the platform enables the government to monitor and respond to data breaches involving official domains.

item.title: Fixing an eMachines EL1200 BIOS bug with Claude
item.description: The author shares their experience using AI to resolve a BIOS bug on an eMachines EL1200, building on their history of hacking legacy hardware. The piece highlights how modern LLMs can assist in troubleshooting complex firmware and technical configuration issues.

item.title: A Syncthing and SQLite Gotcha
item.description: This post explains the technical risks associated with using Syncthing to synchronize SQLite databases. It highlights how the 'rename' system call can lead to data corruption when file synchronization conflicts with database write operations.
